heading: Data and credits
intro: AER is built on archived NASA mission data. Nothing is live: all data was downloaded before the hackathon and bundled with the app.

dataSources.what: Base map photo and terrain (elevation, slope, shaded relief)
dataSources.product: Mars 2020 Terrain Relative Navigation HiRISE DTM and orthomosaic
THEMIS-derived thermal inertia of Jezero crater
dataSources.credit: C. S. Edwards and J. Buz

dataSources.what: Weather: pressure, air and ground temperature, wind
dataSources.provider: NASA Planetary Data System, Atmospheres Node

dataSources.product: Mastcam-Z visible aerosol optical depth record (preliminary)
Solar radiation on Mars: Update 1990 (NASA TM-103623)
dataSources.provider: J. Appelbaum and D. J. Flood

dataSources.what: Rover route, waypoints and sample sites
dataSources.product: Mars 2020 waypoints and traverse; Mars rock samples list

imageCredits: Earth on the title screen: NASA, Apollo 17 crew, photo AS17-148-22727 (December 7, 1972)
fiction: The AER-1 lander, its crew, its supplies and tank, the rover's beacon and the radio bridge are game fiction. Perseverance, Ingenuity, the landing hardware, the sample sites and all data layers are real.
aiDisclosure: The AER-1 lander image was generated with AI and carries a visible watermark.
Parts of the code, the data pipeline and the game text were written with help from AI assistants (Claude and Antigravity). All data values come from the sources above, not from AI.
noAffiliation: AER is a NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 entry. It is not endorsed by NASA and uses no NASA logos.
